He said that the kingdom of the Babylonians was a lioness, that of the Persians a bear, and that of the Greeks a leopard. Why then did he not say what kind of beast the kingdom of the Romans was? Instead he says only that it was "terrifying and exceedingly dreadful; its teeth were of iron and its claws of bronze." Understand, O man, and glorify the Lord. The Babylonians were a single nation, though in those times they seemed to rule over everyone. So he rightly named them a lioness, as an animal of a single kind. Likewise the Persians are a single nation, filthy indeed, but of one language, and for this reason he compared them to a bear. In the same way he called the Greeks a leopard, for they were all Greeks. But the beast that rules now is not one nation. It gathers to itself people of every language and every race and prepares them as a force for battle. They are all called Romans, but they do not all come from one country. So the prophet did well: struck with amazement as he foresaw what was to come, he did not name what kind of beast it was. Instead he marveled, saying: "My spirit shuddered within me, I, Daniel, and the visions of my head troubled me. I approached one of those standing there and asked him the exact truth about all this. He told me the exact truth and made known to me the interpretation of the words." Who, then, were those standing there, if not the angels who stand before the face of the Lord's glory and render him unceasing service, always ready to carry out his commands?

But a thought has come into my heart, and I will not leave it unspoken, since it can benefit the soul. The Lord was born in the forty-second year of Augustus Caesar, the time from which the Roman Empire flourished. Through the apostles the Lord called all nations and all languages and made them a nation of faithful Christians, who bear in their hearts the Lord's new name. In the same way the kingdom that now rules by the working of Satan imitated this as a rival. It too gathers the bravest men from all the nations and fits them out for war, calling them Romans. This is also why the first census took place under Augustus, when the Lord was born in Bethlehem: so that the people of this world, enrolled under an earthly king, might be called Romans, while those who believe in the heavenly King might be named Christians, bearing on their foreheads the trophy of victory over death.

But let us not stray from our subject. Let it be shown that what the prophet saw is true and that what we, by the Lord's grace, have understood and said is accurate. Let us see whether the angel who instructed the blessed Daniel bears witness to our words. For he says: "These four beasts are four kingdoms that will arise on the earth, and they will be taken away. And the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it for ever and ever." This must be so. Three of the beasts have already run their course and passed away, as was shown above, and one is still at its height. When this one too is removed, earthly things will come to an end and heavenly things will begin. Then the kingdom of the saints, indestructible and eternal, will be revealed. The heavenly King will be shown openly to all, no longer seen in a form as on Mount Sinai, nor revealed in a pillar of cloud on a mountaintop. He will come with powers and armies of angels, God made flesh and man, Son of God and of man, coming from heaven as judge of the world. He will remove all the kingdoms of this world. He will thresh them, winnow them and scatter them like dust from a threshing floor in summer, and he will give the kingdom to the saints of the Most High. He will gather the wheat into his granary and burn the chaff with unquenchable fire. He is now despised by the godless and the impious and blasphemed by unbelievers, who understand neither what is written nor to whom the authority to judge has been given. Even if he now delays, unwilling to bring judgment on the world before the appointed time, and so carries out his own Father's command, he will surely come with his armies and repay each one according to his deeds.

All of you who draw near to God with reverence, recognize him who long ago was shown to the people by Moses, was revealed on the mountain, was proclaimed beforehand by the prophets, and was seen by the blessed Daniel in human form. Of him Daniel says: "I watched in the vision of the night, and behold, one like a son of man was coming with the clouds of heaven. He came to the Ancient of Days and was presented before him. To him were given dominion and honor and the kingdom, and all peoples, tribes and languages will serve him. His authority is an everlasting authority that will not pass away, and his kingdom will not be destroyed." By "the Ancient of Days" he means none other than the Lord, God and Master of all, who is also the Father of Christ himself. He makes the days grow old, and he himself is not made old by times or days. Of him it was said above: "Thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took his seat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool. His throne was a flame of fire, and its wheels were burning fire. A river of fire streamed out before him. A thousand thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court sat, and books were opened." To him the Son of Man was presented, borne on a cloud and brought forward by archangels, to receive from him all dominion, authority, power and kingship, so that all peoples, tribes and languages should serve him. And so that no one should suppose that the kingdom given to him by the Father is temporary or earthly, the prophet says: "His authority is an everlasting authority that will not pass away, and his kingdom will not be destroyed." The Father subjected all things to his own Son, things in heaven, things on earth and things under the earth. In all of these he showed him to be the firstborn in everything. He is firstborn from God, so that he might be shown to be Son of God, second after the Father. He is firstborn before the angels, so that he might be shown to be Lord of the angels too. He is firstborn from a virgin, so that he might be shown to be refashioning in himself Adam, the first man to be formed. He is also firstborn from the dead, so that he himself might become the firstfruits of our resurrection.

Since, then, all the prophets and apostles bear witness to him, while the lawless in their disobedience blaspheme him, scorn what has been spoken, persecute and oppress his servants, and do not expect these things, as though they will never come to pass, let us look into them: we who believe in the word of truth, who are led by the Word himself to eternal life, taught by the prophets and enlightened by the Spirit. Then, made wise by his grace, we may come to know the things that were proclaimed long ago and that have come to pass, and will come to pass, in their appointed times. And keeping God's judgment before our eyes, let us guard ourselves from every evil, so that we may escape the eternal fire and the unceasing punishment. For even if these things are not happening now in our own day, because the times are not yet fulfilled, we must still pray that we may not be found in those times when they will come to pass. Otherwise someone may grow faint under the great tribulation that is coming upon the world and fall away from eternal life. For we must look closely at what the prophet says: "And I sought to know precisely about the fourth beast, for it was different from every other beast, exceedingly terrible; its teeth were of iron and its claws of bronze; it devoured and crushed, and trampled what was left with its feet. And I sought to know about the ten horns on its head, and about the other horn that came up and shook out three of the earlier ones, the horn that had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and whose appearance [was] greater than the rest. I watched, and that horn made war with the saints and prevailed against them, until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the saints of the Most High, and the time arrived, and the saints took possession of the kingdom." As we said earlier, then, he is pointing to this fourth kingdom, and no other kingdom greater than it, or even like it, has arisen on the earth. From it ten horns are to spring up. For it will be divided into ten diadems, and among them another little horn will come up, which is that of the Antichrist. It will uproot three of those before it: that is, he will do away with the three kings of Egypt, of the Libyans, and of the Ethiopians, wishing to secure the whole kingdom for himself. Once he has gained mastery over the remaining seven horns, he will be puffed up by the alien and evil spirit within him. Then he begins to stir up war against the saints and to persecute everyone everywhere, wishing to be glorified and worshiped by all as God. As Ezekiel too says of him: "Because your heart was lifted up and you said, 'I am God'"; and again: "Will you indeed say to those who slay you, 'I am God'? But you are a man and not God." And Isaiah likewise: "But you said in your mind, 'I will ascend to heaven; I will set my throne above the clouds of heaven; I will sit on the holy mountain; I will be like the Most High.'"

If anyone wishes to read about him in detail, these things have been set out more clearly in another book, so that we need not discuss him a second time. For now, in keeping with our present subject, we will speak about the beast that exists at present. For Daniel speaks thus: "And the angel said to me: The fourth beast shall be a fourth kingdom on the earth, which shall surpass all the kingdoms. It shall devour the whole earth and trample it and break it in pieces. And as for its ten horns, ten kings shall arise, and after them another shall arise, who shall surpass in evil all who were before him. He shall speak words against the Most High, and shall lead astray the saints of the Most High, and shall think to change times and law; and it shall be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time. And the court sat, and they shall take away his dominion, to destroy it and abolish it to the end. And the kingdom and the authority and the greatness of the kings under the whole heaven were given to the saints of the Most High; and his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him." Here is the end of the account.

The prophet wished to persuade us in every way and to bring us to the truth of what he had seen. So he asks one of the angels standing by, so that he himself might be instructed more exactly about the fourth beast: "For I sought," he says, "to know more precisely about it, for it was terrible and astounding." The angel instructs him, or rather through him persuades us too to believe what he had rightly seen. He recounts to him everything that is to happen in the last times: the division of the fourth beast into the ten horns that arise from it, the appearance of the Antichrist among them, his war against the saints, and how long he will hold power. "For it shall be given into his hand," he says, "until a time and times and half a time," which means three and a half years. After this comes the judgment that is to be: "For thrones were set," he says, "and the court sat, and the kingdom was given to the saints of the Most High, and the body of the beast was given over to be burned with fire." For the time has arrived, that is, the whole span of time has been fulfilled, and the saints will possess the kingdom. Then at last the Judge of judges and King of kings comes from heaven. He will take away all the dominion and power of the adversary and will burn them all up, punishing the unrighteous with eternal fire; but to his servants, the prophets and martyrs and all who fear him, he will give the eternal kingdom. As the prophet says: "Here is the end of the account. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts greatly troubled me, and my countenance was changed, and I kept the matter in my heart."

Everyone who reads the divine Scriptures, then, ought to imitate the prophet Daniel and not be rash and hasty, seeking the time before its time and longing to see the unripe figs on the fig tree. Instead he should hold the mystery of God in his heart with fear, lest he be ensnared by his own lips and become answerable for his own soul. For the time will come when the almond tree blossoms, and the caper-berry grows rough, and the locust multiplies, and the fig tree puts forth shoots, and the fruits of apostasy ripen. Then the door of life will be shut, and the pitcher will be shattered at the spring, and the wheel will crash down into the cistern, and the women who grind will cease because they have become few. All will rise up at the voice of the sparrow, and all the daughters of song will be troubled, and the mourners will gather in the marketplace, and a man will go away to his eternal home.

But someone will say: "And when will these things be? At what time or season is the deceiver to be revealed? And what is the day of the Lord's appearing?" The disciples likewise sought to learn these things from the Lord, but he hid the day from them. He did this to make them, and everyone else, watchful for what is to come, always anxious and expecting the heavenly Bridegroom day by day. Otherwise people might neglect his commands because of the long delay, doze off while he tarries, and fall away from heavenly life. For he says: "Keep awake, for you do not know on what day or at what hour your Lord is coming, whether in the evening, or at midnight, or in the morning." Therefore he says: "Blessed is that servant whom his master finds awake when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will set him over all his possessions. But if the wicked servant says in his heart, 'My master is delayed in coming,' and begins to beat the menservants and maidservants and to eat and drink with the drunkards, his master will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know. He will cut him in two and assign him his place with the unbelievers; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Therefore I tell you: keep awake." Our Lord himself declared these things in the Gospel when he was teaching his disciples. Likewise after his resurrection the disciples came to him and asked him the same things, saying: "Lord, are you restoring the kingdom to Israel at this time?" And he said to them: "It is not for you to know the times or seasons that the Father has set by his own authority. But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in Galilee, and in all the country of Samaria, and to the end of the earth."

He hid the day from them, then, but he made it known through the signs that would occur, by which a person may easily recognize it. So we ought to understand what happens in its own time and, knowing it, keep silent. These things must happen even if we do not wish them to, for the truth never lies. He said about the city of Jerusalem, "When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near," and what was spoken came upon it. In the same way we must now expect what is to come. "For when you see," he says, "the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place (let the reader understand), then let those in Judea flee to the mountains. Let the one on the housetop not come down to take anything out of his house, and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak. And woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days. For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world, nor ever will be. And if those days had not been cut short, no flesh would be saved." By this, then, he made it plain to us, so that we should no longer be in doubt about anything. And again he says: "When you see the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place, and when you see the fig tree putting forth its leaves, you know that summer is near. So also, when you see all these things happening, know that he is near, at the very doors." The abomination has not yet come, and the fourth beast alone still holds power. How, then, can the appearing of the Lord take place? But someone will say: "It is written: When you see wars and upheavals, then know that it is near." Yes, it is written. For "nation will rise against nation," he says, "and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be earthquakes in various places, and famines and plagues." These things have already happened and will happen again. "But all these are the beginning of birth pains," he says; the end is not yet among them. "For first the gospel of the Lord must be preached in the whole world as a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come," when the whole span of time has been fulfilled.

Let me also relate what happened not long ago in Syria. A certain man who presided over the church there did not read the divine Scriptures diligently or follow the voice of the Lord. He was led astray himself and led others astray. The Lord had said: "Many false christs and false prophets will arise and will perform signs and wonders, so as to lead astray even the elect, if that were possible. Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ,' or 'Here he is,' do not believe it. If they say, 'Look, he is in the wilderness,' do not go out; if they say, 'Look, he is in the inner rooms,' do not go in." That man did not understand this, and he persuaded many of the brethren to go out into the wilderness with their wives and children to meet Christ. They wandered aimlessly over the mountains and along the roads, so that they were very nearly all arrested as bandits and put to death by the governor. They escaped only because his wife happened to be a believer; at her entreaty he suppressed the matter, so that a persecution of everyone might not arise on their account. How great was their folly and ignorance, to go into the wilderness seeking Christ! It was just as in the time of the prophet Elisha, when the sons of the prophets searched the mountains for three days for Elijah after he had been taken up. The Lord had said, "As the lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man." By this he meant that he would come from heaven plainly and openly, with power and with his Father's glory. Yet these people were looking for him in the mountains and in the wilderness. For his second coming will not be like the first. Then he appeared only as a lowly man, but now he comes as judge of the whole world. Then he came to save humankind, but now he comes to punish all sinners and those who have acted impiously against him. We say these things to strengthen the faithful brethren, so that they may not try to anticipate the counsel of God. Each one should know that on whatever day he departs from this world, he has already been judged, for the end has already come upon him.

There was likewise another man in Pontus, who also presided over a church. He was a devout and humble man, but he did not pay careful attention to the Scriptures, trusting rather in the visions he himself saw. Since he had proved right in one dream, then a second, then a third, he began to foretell things to the brethren as a prophet: "I saw this, and this is going to happen." And once, being led astray, he said: "Know, brethren, that the judgment is going to take place in a year." Those who heard him predicting that the day of the Lord was at hand prayed to the Lord night and day with weeping and lamentation, keeping the coming day of judgment before their eyes. He brought the brethren to such fear and dread that they left their lands and fields untilled, and most of them sold off their possessions. And he said to them: "If it does not happen as I have said, then do not believe even the Scriptures any longer, but let each of you do as he pleases." They waited for the outcome, but the year passed and nothing he had said came to pass. He himself was put to shame as a liar, the Scriptures were shown to be true, and the brethren were left scandalized. So from then on their virgins married and the men went back to farming, and those who had sold their possessions for nothing were later found begging.

These things happen to simple and frivolous people who do not pay careful attention to the Scriptures. They are more readily persuaded by human traditions, by their own errors and dreams, and by myths and old wives' tales. Something similar happened to the children of Israel: they scorned the law of God and set it aside, but gladly submitted to the traditions of the elders. And even now some dare to do the same, giving heed to empty visions and to the teachings of demons. They often prescribe a fast on the Sabbath and on the Lord's day, which Christ did not prescribe, and so dishonor the gospel of Christ.

The words of the Lord are true, but every man is a liar, as it is written. Let us see, then, whether the apostle Paul also agrees with the Lord's words. He wrote to the Thessalonians, urging them always to keep watch and to persevere in prayer, but not yet to expect the day of judgment, since the time had not yet been fulfilled. He said this [to them]: "We ask you, brethren, concerning the coming of the Lord, not to be disturbed either by word or by letter as if from us, as though the day of the Lord were at hand. Let no one deceive you in any way. For that day will not come unless the apostasy comes first and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition. He opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God. Do you not remember that I told you these things when I was still with you? And now you know what is restraining him, so that he may be revealed in his own time. For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only there is one who restrains it now, until he is taken out of the way. And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will slay with the breath of his mouth and destroy by the manifestation of his coming. The coming of the lawless one is according to the working of Satan." Who, then, is the one who restrains until now, if not the fourth beast? When it has been removed and taken out of the way, the deceiver will come. But no doubt, being curious, you ask how many years remain for the beast before it is taken away. You do not realize that by asking this you are seeking danger for yourself and longing to see the judgment sooner. For "woe," he says, "to those who long for the day of the Lord! It is darkness and not light. It is as if a man fled from a lion and a bear met him, and he rushed into his house and leaned his hands against the wall, and a snake bit him. Is not the day of the Lord like this, darkness and not light, gloom with no brightness?"

Why should you busy yourself with the times and try to find out the day of the Lord, when the Savior has hidden it from us? Tell me, do you know the day of your own departure, that you should pry into the end of the whole world? If God were not patient with us because of his surpassing compassion, everything would have been wiped out long ago. Read what was said [also] by John in the Revelation: "And I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been beheaded for the name of Jesus. They cried out to God and said, 'How long, O Lord our God, will you refrain from judging and avenging our blood on those who dwell on the earth?' And they were given white robes and told to wait a little while longer, until their fellow servants, who were to be killed as they had been, should complete their witness." The martyrs shed their own blood for Christ, and yet they were commanded to be patient. Why, then, are you not patient too, so that others also may be saved and the number of the called and of the saints may be completed?

But we do not want to leave even this subject without proof, since human beings are so greedy to know. So we are compelled to say, against our will, what is not permitted to be said. The years counted from the foundation of the world and from Adam make clear to us what is being sought. The first coming of our Lord, his coming in the flesh, when he was born in Bethlehem, took place four days before the Nones of April [eight days before the Kalends of January], on a Wednesday, in the forty-second year of the reign of Augustus, which was the five thousand five hundredth year from Adam. And he suffered in his thirty-[third] year, eight days before the Kalends of April, on a Friday, the day of Preparation, in the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar, when Rufus and Rubellio were consuls [and Gaius Caesar for the fourth time and Gaius Cestius Saturninus]. So the six thousand years must necessarily be completed before the Sabbath can come: the rest, the holy day on which God rested from all the works that he had begun to make. The Sabbath is a type and image of the coming kingdom of the saints, when they will reign with Christ after he comes from heaven, as John [too] relates in his Revelation. For a day of the Lord is like a thousand years. Since God made all things in six days, the six thousand years must be completed. They have not yet been completed, as John says: "Five have fallen, one is" (that is, the sixth), "the other has not yet come." By "the other" he means the seventh, in which the rest will come.

But someone will surely say, "How will you prove to me that the Savior was born in the five thousand five hundredth year?" You can learn it easily, my friend. The things that Moses made long ago in the wilderness for the tabernacle were carried out as types and images of spiritual mysteries, so that when the truth came in Christ in the last times, you would be able to understand that these things had been fulfilled. For God says to him, "You shall make the ark of incorruptible wood, and you shall overlay it with pure gold inside and out; and you shall make it two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high." Added together, these measurements make five and a half cubits, to show the five thousand five hundred years. At that time the Savior came from the Virgin and brought into the world the ark, his own body, overlaid with pure gold: within by the Word, and without by the Holy Spirit. So the truth has been demonstrated and the ark made plain. From the birth of Christ, then, we must count the remaining five hundred years to complete the six thousand years, and so the end will come. That the Savior was present in the world in the fifth and a half age, bearing the incorruptible ark, his own body, John tells us when he says, "It was the sixth hour," to show the half of the day. Now a day of the Lord is a thousand years, and half of that is five hundred. It was not fitting for him to come sooner, for the burden of the law still remained; nor yet when the sixth day had been completed, for then the washing is closed. He came in the fifth and a half, so that in the remaining half of the time the gospel might be preached to the whole world, and when the sixth day was complete he might bring the present life to an end. For since the Persians held power and reigned for two hundred and thirty years, and after them the Greeks, being more glorious, for three hundred years, the fourth beast, strong and greater than all that were before it, must of necessity reign for five hundred years. When these times are completed and the ten horns rise from it in the last days, the Antichrist will appear among them, of whom we have spoken earlier. When he wages war and persecutes the saints, then we must look for the appearing of the Lord from heaven, so that the King of kings may be openly shown to all, and the Judge of judges may be made known as he comes with boldness and glory. For everything that God has already foreordained to happen, and that has been proclaimed beforehand by the prophets, will be fulfilled in this way at its own proper time.

So the prophet, having finished with the subject before him and having taught us with all precision the certainty of what is to come, turned again to the kingdoms of the Persians and the Greeks and related another vision to us, which came to pass and was fulfilled in its own times. His purpose was that, having made us believers by this, he might present us to God as still more faithful with regard to what is yet to happen. He says: "In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one that had appeared to me at first. I was in Susa the citadel, which is in the land of Elam, and I was by the Ulai. I raised my eyes and looked, and behold, a ram was standing by the Ulai, and it had high horns, and one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up last. I saw the ram butting toward the sea, the north, and the south, and no beasts could stand before it, and there was no one who could rescue from its hand; it did as it pleased and became great. And as I was considering, behold, a he-goat came from the southwest across the face of the whole earth, and the goat had a horn between its eyes. It came to the ram that had the horns, which I had seen standing before the Ulai, and ran at it in the fury of its strength. I saw it reach the ram, and it was enraged against it and struck the ram and shattered both its horns, and the ram had no strength to stand before it. It threw it down to the ground and trampled it, and there was no one to rescue the ram from its hand. The he-goat became exceedingly great, and when it was strong its great horn was broken, and four horns came up in its place toward the four winds of heaven. Out of one of them came a single strong horn, and it grew exceedingly great toward the south and toward the power; it grew great as far as the host of heaven, and some of the host and of the stars fell to the earth, and it trampled them. And until the chief commander rescues the captivity; and because of him the sacrifice was disturbed, and it came about and prospered for him, and the sanctuary will be made desolate. Sin was set upon the sacrifice, and righteousness was thrown to the ground, and he acted and prospered. Then I heard a holy one speaking, and one holy one said to a certain one who was speaking, 'How long will the vision stand, with the sacrifice taken away and the sin of desolation set up, and the sanctuary and the host trampled underfoot?' And he said to him, 'Until evening and morning, one thousand three hundred days, and the sanctuary will be taken away.'"

What he had related in the first vision he now explains a second time, for the building up of believers. By the ram butting toward the sea, the north, and the south he means Darius, king of the Persians, who prevailed over all the nations; for, he says, "no beasts could stand before it." By the he-goat coming from the southwest he means Alexander of Macedon, king of the Greeks. The goat coming to the ram, being enraged against it, striking it in the face, shattering it, throwing it to the ground, and trampling it signifies what actually happened: Alexander joined battle with Darius, overpowered him, and prevailed over his whole force, destroying and trampling his army. Then, after the he-goat was exalted, its great horn was broken, and four horns came up in its place toward the four winds of heaven. For Alexander, after conquering the whole land of Persia and subduing its people, afterwards died, having divided his kingdom into four dominions, as was shown above, that is, to Seleucus, Demetrius, Ptolemy, and Philip. From these one horn was raised up and grew great as far as the host of heaven. "And because of him," he says, "the sacrifice was disturbed, and righteousness was thrown to the ground." For Antiochus, called Epiphanes, who was of Alexander's line, became king. After reigning over Syria and bringing all Egypt under his control, he later went up against Jerusalem, entered the sanctuary, and took all the treasures in the house of the Lord, together with the golden lampstand, the table, and the altar. He carried out a great slaughter in the land, spoke arrogant words, and put a stop to sacrifice and offering; he built shrines and idol temples throughout the city, and they sacrificed swine and unclean beasts. This was to fulfill what the prophet said: "And because of him the sacrifice was disturbed, and righteousness was thrown to the ground, and the sanctuary and the host will be trampled underfoot until evening and morning, one thousand three hundred days." For at that time it came about that the sanctuary remained desolate for three and a half years, so that one thousand three hundred days were completed, until Judas Maccabeus rose up after the death of his father Mattathias, resisted him, cut down the armies of Antiochus, and freed the city. They recovered the sanctuary and rededicated it, doing everything according to the law.

That these things truly came to pass as described, Daniel himself bears witness. He says: "And when I saw the vision, I sought understanding, and behold, there stood before me one with the appearance of a man. And I heard a man's voice between the banks of the Ulai, and he called out and said, 'Gabriel, make this man understand the vision.' And he came and stood near where I was standing, and when he came I was terrified and fell on my face. He said to me, 'Understand, son of man, for the vision is for the time of the end.' And as he was speaking with me I was terrified and fell on my face to the ground. He touched me and set me on my feet and said, 'Behold, I am making known to you what will be at the end of the wrath, for the vision is for the time of the end. The ram that you saw, the one with the horns, is the king of the Persians and Medes. The he-goat is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn that was between its eyes is the first king. As for the one that was broken, in whose place four horns stood up: four kings will arise from his nation, but not with his strength. And at the end of their reign, when their sins are complete, a king will arise, shameless of face and skilled in riddles. His strength will be mighty, though not by his own strength, and he will cause astonishing destruction; he will succeed and act. He will destroy the mighty and the holy people, and the yoke of his collar will prosper. Deceit will be in his hand, and he will magnify himself in his heart; by deceit he will destroy many, and he will stand for the ruin of many, and he will crush them like eggs in his hand. The vision of the evening and the morning that has been told is true. But you, seal up the vision, for it is for many days.' And I, Daniel, fell asleep and was sick; then I rose and went about the king's business, and I was astonished at the vision, and there was no one who understood it."

Since, then, the angel Gabriel explained these things to the prophet just as we have understood them, and as they actually came to pass and are all clearly recorded in the books of the Maccabees, let us also see what he says about the weeks. Daniel had read the book of the prophet Jeremiah, in which it is written that the sanctuary would be desolate for seventy years, and with fasting and supplication he confessed and pleaded that the people might return all the sooner from captivity to the city of Jerusalem. He tells it as follows: "In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, who became king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans, I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of the years, according to the word of the Lord that came to the prophet Jeremiah, for the completion of the desolation of Jerusalem: seventy years. And I turned my face to the Lord my God to seek him with prayer and supplications, with fasting and sackcloth. I prayed to the Lord my God and made confession, and I said: 'O Lord, the great and wonderful God, who keeps your covenant and mercy with those who love you and keep your commandments, we have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted lawlessly; we have rebelled and turned aside from your commandments and from your judgments. We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our rulers, our fathers, and all the people of the land. To you, O Lord, belongs righteousness, and to us shame of face, as it is this day, to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.'"

He relates these things as a confession made on behalf of the people, declaring the sins of the people and of their fathers, who did not listen to his servants the prophets, who were sent to them to speak in the name of the Lord. And while he was setting forth his whole supplication in humility, with fasting and sackcloth, the angel Gabriel was sent to him to give him understanding of what he was seeking. For Daniel says: "While I was still speaking and praying and confessing my sins and the sins of my people, and laying my plea before the Lord my God for the holy mountain, while I was still speaking in prayer, behold, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, came flying, and he touched me at about the hour of the evening sacrifice. He gave me understanding and spoke with me and said, 'Daniel, I have now come out to give you understanding. At the beginning of your supplication a word went out, and I have come to tell it to you, for you are a man of desires.'"

See how the prophet likened the swiftness of the angels to a winged bird, because of the lightness and nimbleness of the angels, who are spirits flying swiftly and obeying whatever they are commanded. As Solomon says: "Do not curse the king in your bedchamber, lest a winged bird carry your words to him." Gabriel the angel, then, says to him: "From the day you set your face to humble yourself before the Lord your God, your supplication was heard, and I was sent to give you understanding, so that you might not seek a time before its time. For you are a man of desires; you desire to see these things which are about to be made known to you through me, but they will be fulfilled in their own time." And he went on to say: "Seventy weeks have been decreed for your people and for the holy city, to bring sins to an end, to seal up sins, to wipe out iniquities, to make atonement for lawless deeds, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint the Holy of Holies. And you shall know and understand: from the going forth of the words to answer and to build Jerusalem until an anointed leader there are seven weeks and sixty-two weeks." Having named seventy weeks, then, he divided them into two, so that what he was telling the prophet might be better understood. For he says, "until an anointed leader, seven weeks," which is forty-nine years. For Daniel saw these things in Babylon in the twenty-first year. When the forty-nine years are added to the twenty-first year, the seventy years are completed of which the blessed prophet Jeremiah spoke, saying that the sanctuary would be desolate for seventy years from the captivity that befell them under Nebuchadnezzar, and that after this the people would return, and sacrifice and offering would be made, with an anointed one as their leader. And what anointed one does he mean, if not Jesus son of Jozadak, who returned with the people at that time and, when the sanctuary had been rebuilt in the seventieth year, offered sacrifice according to the law? For all the kings and priests were called "anointed" because they were anointed with the holy oil that Moses had prepared long ago. They bore the title of lordship upon themselves, foreshadowing the type and displaying the image beforehand, until the perfect King and Priest, Christ, came from heaven, who alone did the will of the Father, as it is written in the Books of Kings: "And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who will do everything according to my heart."

So, to show the time when he would come, whom the blessed Daniel longed to see, he says: "And after the seven weeks, another sixty-two weeks," which comprise a period of four hundred and thirty-four years. For after the people returned from Babylon under the leadership of Jesus son of Jozadak, Ezra the scribe, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, who was of the tribe of Judah, four hundred and thirty-four years passed until the coming of Christ, so that the Priest of priests might appear in the world, and the one who takes away the sins of the world might be openly displayed, as John says of him: "Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world." Gabriel likewise says, "to wipe out iniquities and to make atonement for sins." And who wiped out our iniquities? Paul the apostle teaches you, saying: "He himself became our peace, who made both one and broke down the dividing wall of the partition, the enmity, in his flesh, abolishing the law of commandments expressed in ordinances, and wiping out the record of sins that stood against us, which was hostile to us; and he took it out of the way, nailing it to the cross." So it is "to wipe out iniquities and to make atonement for iniquities." And who are those who obtain atonement for their iniquities, if not those who believe in his name and seek his favor by good works?

That four hundred and thirty-four years passed from the return of the people from Babylon until the birth of Christ is easy to understand from what has been set out. Since the first covenant was given to the children of Israel after four hundred and thirty-four years, it was necessary that the second also be fixed by the same span of time, so that it might be awaited by the people and easily recognized by those who believe. That is why Gabriel says, "and to anoint the Holy of Holies." No one is Holy of Holies except the Son of God alone, who, when he came and showed that he was the one anointed by the Father and sent into the world, said to them: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach good news to the poor, to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord." All who believed in the heavenly Priest were cleansed by that Priest himself, and their sins were wiped out; but all who disbelieved him, despising him as a mere man, had their sins sealed up as beyond removal. Therefore the angel, foreseeing that not all would believe in him, said, "to bring sins to an end and to seal up sins." For those who disobeyed him to the end had their sins brought to completion and sealed, kept for judgment; but those who were going to believe in him and confess to him as the one able to forgive sins had their sins wiped out.

And that is why he says, "and to seal up vision and prophet." Since he himself had come as the fulfillment of the law and the prophets — for "the law and the prophets were until John" — what they had spoken had to be sealed, so that at the coming of the Lord everything might be loosed and brought to light, what had been sealed and could not be known might be easily understood, and what had long been bound might now be loosed by him. So the Lord himself spoke to the rulers of the people, who were indignant when they saw him performing mighty works on the Sabbath day and healing every disease and every infirmity. He said to them: "Hypocrites! Does not each of you untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to water it? And ought not this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound for eighteen years, be loosed on the Sabbath day?" All those, then, whom Satan had bound in his snares, the Lord came and loosed from the bonds of death, binding the strong one who was against us and setting humanity free. As Isaiah also says: "Then he will say to those in bonds, 'Come out,' and to those in darkness, 'Be enlightened.'" And that all that was spoken long ago through the law and the prophets was sealed and unknown to people, Isaiah says: "And they will give the sealed book to a man who knows letters and say to him, 'Read this,' and he will say, 'I cannot read it, for it is sealed.'" This had to be so: what was spoken long ago through the prophets had to be sealed to the unbelieving Pharisees, who thought they knew the letter of the law, but opened in its entirety to those who believe.

So what was sealed long ago has now, through the grace of the Lord, all been opened to the saints. For he himself was the perfect seal and the key of David, "who opens and no one shuts, and shuts and no one opens." As John also says: "And I saw in the right hand of the one seated on the throne a book written inside and out, sealed with seven seals. And I saw an angel proclaiming with a loud voice, 'Who is worthy to open the book and to loose its seals?' And no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the book or to look into it. And many were weeping, because no one was found worthy to open the book or to look into it. And one of the elders said to me, 'Do not weep. Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root and Offspring of David, has conquered, so that he can open the book and loose its seven seals.' And I saw in the midst of the throne and in the midst of the elders a Lamb standing as though slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth. And he came and took the book from the right hand of the one seated on the throne. And when he took the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each holding a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints. And they sing a new song, saying, 'You are worthy to take the book and to open its seals, for you were slain, and by your blood you purchased us for God from every tribe and tongue and people and nation, and you have made them a kingdom and priests to our God, and they will reign on the earth.'" So he took the book and loosed it, so that what had been spoken of him in secret long ago might now be proclaimed openly from the housetops. That is why the angel said to Daniel, "Seal up these words, for the vision is for the time of the end"; but to Christ it was not said, "Seal," but rather, "Loose what was bound long ago," so that through his grace we might come to know the will of the Father and believe in the one whom he sent for the salvation of humankind, Jesus Christ our Lord.

So he says, “And it will return and be rebuilt, street and wall.” And this really happened, for the people returned and built the city, the temple and the wall all around it. Then he says: “After the sixty-two weeks the times will run out, and one week will make a covenant with many; and in the middle of the week sacrifice and libation will be taken away, and upon the temple will be the abomination of desolations.” For when the sixty-two weeks have been fulfilled, and Christ has come, and the gospel has been preached in every place, and the times have run out, one week will remain, the last. In it Elijah and Enoch will be present, and in the middle of it the abomination of desolation will appear, the Antichrist, proclaiming desolation to the world. When he comes, the sacrifice and libation that are now offered to God by the nations in every place will be taken away.

After this, the prophet again describes to us another vision. Blessed Daniel cared for nothing else than to be taught everything about the future accurately, so that he might in turn be seen to teach us. So he says: “In the third year of Cyrus king of the Persians a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar, and the word was true; and great power and understanding were given to him in the vision. In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks of days. I ate no pleasant bread, no meat or wine entered my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until three weeks of days were completed. On the twenty-fourth day of the first month…” “I humbled myself,” he says, “for twenty-one days, praying to the living God and asking him for a revelation of mysteries.” And the Father heard him and sent his own Word, to show through him what was going to happen. And this took place by the great river, for the Child had to be shown there, where he was also going to forgive sins. “And I lifted up my eyes,” he says, “and looked, and behold, a man clothed in baddin.” In the first vision he says, “Behold, the angel Gabriel flying,” but here it is not so: he sees the Lord himself, not yet fully man, but appearing in the form of a man, as he says, “And behold, a man clothed in baddin.” For Christ, clothed in the varied calling of the gifts, displayed a many-coloured tunic of mysteries; the priestly tunic was made of different colours to signify the various nations that were awaiting the coming of Christ, so that we might be equipped with various gifts.

“And his loins were girded with gold of Ophaz.” Ophaz, translated from Hebrew into Greek, means “pure gold.” So he was girded around his loins with a pure belt, for the Word was going to bind all of us around his own body by his own love, as with a belt, and so carry us. For he himself was the perfect body, and we are his members, united as in a perfect body and carried by the Word himself. “And his body was like Tharsis.” Tharsis means “Ethiopians.” For the prophet was already foretelling how hard he would be to recognize, that the Word, when he appeared in the flesh in the world, would be hard for many to know. “And his face was like lightning, and his eyes like flaming torches.” For the fiery and judging nature of the Word had to be signified in advance, so that he might justly bring fire on the ungodly and burn them up, but grant eternal immortality to the righteous and to those who have hoped in him. He adds, “And his arms and feet were like gleaming bronze,” to signify that the first calling, that of the fathers, and the second, that from the Gentiles, are alike. For the last things will be like the first: “I will make your rulers as at the beginning,” he says, “and your leaders as before.” “And the sound of his voice was like the sound of a great multitude.” For today all of us who believe in him utter the words of Christ, speaking, as it were, through his mouth the things he has commanded.

“And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision.” For he reveals himself only to the holy and to those who fear him. If anyone now seems to live as a member of the Church but does not have the fear of God, his fellowship with the saints is of no use to him, since he has not acquired the power of the Spirit within himself. For at that time too there were many standing with Daniel, but they did not see the vision, because they were not worthy; instead a great terror fell on them and they fled in fear. “And I,” he says, “was left alone, and I fell on my face to the ground, and behold, something like a man’s hand touched me.” “A man’s hand,” he says: not yet a man, but by the hand he signifies the dispensation that was to come.

“And he raised me up on my knees and said to me: Daniel, man greatly beloved, understand the words that I am speaking to you; and stand upright, for I have now been sent to you. And when he had spoken this word to me, I stood up trembling, and he said to me: Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before God, your words were heard.” See how much the piety of a righteous man can achieve, that things not yet to be made known in this world should be revealed to him alone as worthy of them. At first he was given understanding by the angel Gabriel; then he was made wise a second time by the Lord himself. For he says: “And I looked, and behold, something like the appearance of a son of man touched me.” First he said, “like a man’s hand,” but now he says, “like the appearance of a son of man,” so as first to show him in part, and the second time his complete incarnation. For the Word of God was proclaimed beforehand as a man in the form of a man, a man who would appear in the flesh in the world, though he was not yet then son of man. But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, born of a woman, so that, having put on the man from the Virgin, he might be shown to be both Son of God and Son of Man. “And I opened my mouth,” he says, “and spoke to the one standing before me: Lord, at your vision my insides were turned within me, and I had no strength.” For at the coming of the Lord the things above had to come down below, so that the things below might also be able to come up to the things above. “And he again touched me,” he says, “like the appearance of a man, and strengthened me, and said to me: Do not be afraid, man greatly beloved; peace be with you; be courageous and be strong.” For when all the strength and glory of our life has failed, then we are strengthened by Christ, who stretches out his hand and raises us up, as the living from the dead and as from Hades to the resurrection of life.

“And as he spoke with me, I grew strong and said: Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.” For once the Word has given us good hope for what is to come, we can easily listen to his voice as well. So he says to him: “Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight with the prince of the Persians; but I will tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth, and there is no one who stands with me in these things except Michael your prince, and him I have left there. For from the day that you set your face to humble yourself before the Lord your God, your prayer was heard, and I was sent to fight with the prince of the Persians.” For a decision had been made not to let the people go. “So that your request might be granted quickly, I opposed him and left Michael your prince there.” And who is Michael but the angel entrusted with the people, as he says to Moses: “I will not go with you on the way, because the people are stiff-necked; but my angel will go with you”? It was he who confronted Moses at the lodging place when he was bringing his uncircumcised child into Egypt. For it was not fitting that Moses, who was becoming the ambassador and mediator of the law and was proclaiming the covenant of the fathers, should bring along an uncircumcised child, lest he be thought by the people a false prophet and a deceiver.

“And now,” he says, “I will tell you the truth.” Could the Truth tell anything other than the truth? The one who appeared to Daniel was the Truth, and he told the truth. And again, appearing in the world as the Truth, he taught the truth. O blessed disciples, taught the truth by Christ! So he says to him: “Behold, three more kings will arise in Persia, and the fourth will gain great wealth, more than all; and after he has become powerful through his wealth, he will rise up against all the kingdoms of the Greeks. And a mighty king will arise, and he will rule with great dominion and do as he pleases; and as soon as his kingdom has arisen it will be broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven.” We have already explained these things above, when we were discussing the four beasts. But since scripture now goes through all this again in detail, we too must necessarily discuss it a second time, so as not to leave the scripture idle and unexplained. “Three more kings,” he says, “will arise in Persia, and the fourth will gain great wealth.” This has happened. For after Cyrus arose Darius, then Artaxerxes, then Xerxes. These three became kings; the scripture has been fulfilled. “And the fourth will gain great wealth.” Who is this but Darius, who reigned and became renowned and grew rich and rose up against all the kingdoms of the Greeks? Against him rose Alexander the Macedonian, the son of Philip, who destroyed his kingdom; and after he had subdued the Persians, his kingdom was divided toward the four winds of heaven. For when Alexander died, he divided his kingdom into four realms.

“And another mighty king will arise and will enter the strongholds of the king of Egypt.” For a certain Antiochus became king of Syria. He began to reign in the one hundred and thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks. At that time he went to war against Ptolemy king of Egypt, overpowered him and defeated him. Returning from Egypt, he went up against Jerusalem in the one hundred and forty-third year, took all the treasures that were in the house of the Lord, and went to Antioch. After these things had happened, two full years later, the king sent his own tribute-collector to the cities of Judea to force the Jews to abandon their ancestral laws and submit to the king’s decrees and laws. When he arrived at the town of Modein, he summoned a certain man named Mattathias, a devout and righteous man of priestly descent, and said to him: “Come now, Mattathias, offer sacrifice and carry out the king’s command, as all the nations have done; for you are a great ruler and leader in the city, supported by sons, and you will be a friend of the king.” But he answered: “Even if all the nations and every man go after the king to do as he commands, I and my house and my father’s house will not do as the king commands. Far be it from us to abandon the law and the covenant of our fathers. We will not listen to the king’s words to turn aside from our way to the right or to the left.” While he was still speaking these words, behold, a Jewish man came forward in front of him to offer sacrifice on the altar at Modein. When Mattathias saw it, he burned with zeal for the law, his heart was stirred, and he gave vent to righteous anger. He ran forward and killed the Jewish man and the king’s officer who was compelling them, tore down the altar, and cried out in the city: “Let everyone who upholds the holy covenant with the Lord come out after me!” And they left everything in the city and fled into the mountains, and a company of men mighty in strength joined him and became his support.

Then the forces stationed in Syria, hearing what had happened, hurried against them and joined battle with them on the sabbath day. But they, fearing the law of God and bound by God’s commandment, did not lift a hand against them, nor throw a stone at them, nor block up their hiding places. And the others answered them and said: “Even now, come out and carry out the king’s command, and you will live.” But they said: “We will not come out, nor will we carry out the king’s command. We will die in our innocence; heaven and earth bear witness for us that you are destroying us unjustly.” Then they fell upon them with fire, slaughter and captivity, and killed about a thousand of them. So what was spoken to blessed Daniel was fulfilled: “And he will come in on his expeditions, and his heart will be lifted up against the holy covenant, and he will want to do everything as he pleases; and my servants will be afflicted and will grow weak through famine, sword and captivity.”

Mattathias and his sons heard of this and mourned for their brothers, and they said to one another: “If we all do as our brothers have done, our enemies will come and quickly wipe us off the land. So if war comes upon us on the sabbath, let us stand and fight for our lives and for our laws.” Then they fell upon them and drove them out of their territory; they entered the city, circumcised all the boys they found uncircumcised, tore down the altars and all the sacred precincts, and the work prospered in their hands. And Daniel says: “And they will be helped with a little help.” For at that time Mattathias arose, and Judas Maccabaeus arose, and they helped them and rescued them from the hand of the Greeks, and what was said in the scripture was fulfilled.

Again he says: “And the daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement with him. And the arms of the one escorting her will not stand, and both she and the one escorting her will be broken and fall.” This too has happened. For a certain Ptolemais, who was then reigning over Egypt, set out with her two sons, Ptolemy and Philometor, to make an agreement with Antiochus king of Syria. When she arrived near Scythopolis, she was killed there, for the one escorting her betrayed her. Then the two brothers went to war with each other, and Philometor was killed, while Ptolemy prevailed. Then there was another clash between Ptolemy and Antiochus. For scripture says: “And the king of the south will rise up against the king of the north, and an offspring from her will rise up.” What offspring is this but Ptolemy, who went to war against Antiochus? Antiochus marched out against him, but failing to overpower him, he fled and returned again to Antioch to gather a larger army. Ptolemy then took all his arms and carried them off to Egypt, and the scripture was fulfilled, as Daniel says: “And he will carry off to Egypt their gods and their molten images and all their precious gold.”

After this Antiochus marched out a second time, stirring up war against him, and defeated Ptolemy. After these events Antiochus rose up again against the children of Israel and sent a certain Nicanor with a large army to make war on the Jews, at the time when Judas was leading the people after the death of his father Mattathias. Nicanor came to Jerusalem and was defeated by Maccabaeus, and this was reported to King Antiochus. When he heard it, he summoned all his forces, gave them a year’s pay, and ordered them to be ready for whatever was needed. But running short of money for the pay, he decided to go to Persia to collect the tribute. As he was about to leave, he summoned one of his friends named Lysias, entrusted to him his own son Antiochus, gave him all the instructions he wished, and ordered him to send an army into Judea and wipe out the nation. So Lysias set out with the boy Antiochus and marched with a large army to make war on Jerusalem. When he arrived, he was defeated by Maccabaeus, and this was reported to Antiochus in Persia: that all the forces sent into Judea had been cut to pieces, that Lysias had marched against them with an army and had been routed before them, that they had grown strong with weapons and all the supplies from all the camps they had destroyed, and that they had fortified Mount Zion and surrounded it with high and great walls. When he heard this, he fell ill from grief, because things had not turned out as he wished, nor had they happened as he intended. As he was about to die, he summoned his friend Philip and gave him the diadem, so that he might hand it on to his son Antiochus. But Philip arrived, entered Antioch, and took the kingdom for himself, since most of the forces were with him. This was reported to Lysias and the boy Antiochus — for Lysias happened to have surrounded Jerusalem with a palisade and was besieging it — that Philip had arrived bearing the diadem and was in control of the city. When he heard this, he was alarmed and said: “Let us give these men our right hands and make peace with them. For the place is strong, and the affairs of the kingdom are pressing upon us.” So he gave them his right hand and departed, and what was said in scripture was fulfilled: “And reports and haste from the east and the west will alarm him.”

After these things scripture says again: “And another king will rise up, and he will prevail over the land; and the king of the south will rise up, and he will take one of his daughters as wife.” For it happened that a certain Alexander, son of Philip, arose. At that time he rose up against Antiochus, made war on him, killed him, and took control of the kingdom. Then he sent to Ptolemy king of Egypt, saying: “Give me your daughter Cleopatra as wife, for behold, I have taken my seat on the throne of my fathers’ kingdom.” So Ptolemy took his daughter, brought her to Ptolemais, and gave her to Alexander as wife; and the scripture was fulfilled, as it says: “And he will take one of his daughters as wife.” And it says: “And he will ruin her, and she will not be his.” Truly this too has been fulfilled. For when Ptolemy had given him his own daughter, on his way back he saw that Alexander’s kingdom was wonderful and glorious, and, coming to covet it, he spoke treacherously to Alexander. And scripture says: “And at one table both kings will speak lies.” For Ptolemy, coveting Alexander’s kingdom, was plotting malice while he ate with him at table, since he was not at one with him. So the scripture is fulfilled. Ptolemy then went to Egypt, raised a large army, and invaded the country while Alexander had gone to Cilicia; for the people of Tarsus and Mallus happened to be in revolt at the time, and he, wanting to put them down, went there in haste, leaving his wife Cleopatra behind. So Ptolemy, entering the country, stationed garrisons in the cities, and having taken control of Judea he came to his own daughter, and sent letters to Demetrius in the islands, saying: “Come out and come here, and I will give you my daughter Cleopatra as wife, because Alexander has sought to kill me.” He invented these words wishing to bring blame on Alexander. So Demetrius came, and Ptolemy took his own daughter, who had been Alexander’s wife, and gave her to him as wife. And what was said is fulfilled: “He will ruin her, and she will not be his, nor will she remain with him.” For both kings, their hearts are set on evil, and at one table both kings will speak lies. When these things had happened, Alexander heard of them and went to war with Ptolemy, but failing to overpower him he fled to the king of the Arabs. The latter cut off Alexander’s head and sent it to Ptolemy, and Ptolemy received it and put on the two diadems, of Syria and of Egypt; but on the third day after putting them on he died. And what was said in the scripture is fulfilled: “And they will not give him the glory of the kingdom.” For he too died and did not receive glory from all as king.

Having thus described the things that have already happened and been accomplished in their own times, the prophet announces to us another mystery, giving an indication of the last times. For he says: “And another king will arise, shameless, and he will exalt himself above every god and magnify himself, and he will speak monstrous things, and he will prosper until the wrath is accomplished; for it is coming to its end. And he will pay no regard to any of the gods of his fathers, nor to the desire of women, and he will pay no regard to any god, for he will magnify himself above all. And in his place he will honour the god Maozim, and a god whom his fathers did not know he will honour with gold and silver and precious stones; and he will increase glory, and he will subject many to them, and he will divide land as gifts. And these will be delivered out of his hand: Edom and Moab and the chief of the sons of Ammon. And he will stretch out his hand over the land, and the land of Egypt will not escape; and he will gain mastery over the hidden treasures of gold and silver and over all the precious things of Egypt, and of the Libyans and the Ethiopians in their strongholds. And he will pitch his tent Ephadano between the seas on the holy mount Sabir, and he will come to his end.”

This, then, is what the prophet relates about the Antichrist: that he will be shameless, a warmonger and a tyrant, daring to exalt himself above every god. Boasting in his own power, sacking the strongholds of cities, and proud of his gold and silver and precious stones, he will speak monstrous words against God, wishing to be worshipped as God by himself alone. No scripture has kept silent about him. The prophets foretold that he would come for the destruction of many, the Lord bore witness to their words, the apostles taught the same things about him, and John in the Revelation disclosed his name in a hidden way through a number. The Lord declared him to be the abomination of desolation, and the apostle taught that he would appear as a son of the devil, by the working of Satan. He will strike the city of the Tyrians and lay it waste. He will make war on the land of Egypt and lay it flat, raze the whole country of the Libyans, and destroy the king of the Ethiopians and his army by the slaughter of the sword. Lifted up above all kings and every god, he will build the city of Jerusalem and raise up the temple that was overthrown. He will give back to the Jews the whole land and its borders, call their people back from slavery among the nations, and present himself to them as king. The disobedient will worship him as God and bend the knee to him, supposing him to be the Christ, because they do not understand what the prophet said: that he is a deceiver and not true. For Jeremiah says: “Because they disobeyed the truth, he will then speak a spirit of error to this people and to Jerusalem.” That is why the apostle, who knew the people's error and the working of Satan that would be in them, said: “When they say, ‘Peace and security,’ then sudden destruction comes upon them, as labor pains come upon a woman with child, and they will not escape.”

He will kill the two witnesses and forerunners of Christ, who proclaim his glorious coming from heaven. As he says through the prophet: “And I will grant my two witnesses, and they will prophesy for one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.” In the same way he said to Daniel: “And one week will confirm a covenant with many, and in the middle of the week my sacrifice and drink offering will be taken away.” This shows that the one week is divided in two. The two witnesses preach for three and a half years, and for the rest of the week the Antichrist makes war on the saints and lays waste the whole world. So what was said will be fulfilled: “And they will set up the abomination of desolation for one thousand two hundred and ninety days. Blessed is the one who endures in Christ and reaches one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days.” For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been since the foundation of the world. Some will be sent here and others there, to every city and country, to kill the faithful. The Jews will rejoice at their destruction, the nations will gloat, and the unbelievers will join with them. The saints will flee from west to east, others will be pursued from the east to the south, and others will hide in the mountains and caves. Everywhere the abomination will make war on them, putting them to death by his decree on sea and on land and squeezing them out of the world by every means. They will be unable to sell any of their own goods or to buy anything from others unless they carry the name of the beast on their hand or bear his mark on their forehead. For then all the faithful will be driven out of every place, dragged from their houses, expelled from the cities, hauled through the public square, punished with every kind of punishment, and cast out of the whole world.

We must therefore look ahead to the affliction and misery that the saints will suffer then, for we ought to infer what is to come from what is already partly happening. Such a storm and turmoil will arise in all the world. All the faithful everywhere will be killed and slaughtered in every city and country. The blood of the righteous will be poured out. People will be burned alive and others thrown to wild beasts. Infants will be murdered in the streets, and all will be cast out unburied and devoured by dogs. Virgins and women will be openly defiled and shamefully abused, people will be seized and carried off, the holy cemeteries will be dug up, remains will be exhumed and scattered over the plain, and blasphemies will be uttered. There will be turmoil in the cities then, as the saints are hunted out of them. There will be turmoil on the roads and in the deserts, as all seek to hide there. There will be turmoil on the sea, as all try to flee by water. There will be turmoil in the islands, as all are searched out there. Then the earth will bear no fruit for the saints. Every city will be uninhabitable, the sea impossible to sail, and the whole world a desert. Some will waste away from famine, others will faint from thirst, and others will die of fear and great affliction. Where will anyone hide then? To whom will he entrust his own children? Where will he carry off his possessions and keep them safe, when he cannot save even his own life? Then there will be much wailing of infants, lamenting of fathers and mothers, shrieking of women and virgins, and mourning of brothers and relatives. Who will mourn for whom then? Brother will not mourn brother, for he himself is waiting for death. Mother will not mourn daughter, for she too sees death coming. Father will not mourn son, for he fears that he too will be killed.

That is why the Lord, foreseeing these things, says: “Pray that your flight may not be in winter or on a sabbath.” He means that you should be neither idle from righteousness, as on a sabbath, nor busy with the affairs of this life, as in winter, so that that day does not come upon you suddenly like a snare. “For if those days had not been cut short,” he says, “no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be cut short.” But “after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will burn as they fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken; and then they will see the Son of Man coming with power and great glory.” The devil received authority for a little while to throw the earth into turmoil, as it is written: “God gave him authority to test those who dwell on the earth.” How much more, then, will the Son of God, who has received all authority over things in heaven, on earth and under the earth, throw the whole world and its elements into turmoil to avenge the saints! He will arrive with the power of angels and the glory of the Father, when he comes to be glorified in all his saints and marveled at in all who call on him, to repay with affliction those who afflict us, and to give relief to us who are afflicted.

Daniel, then, foretold two abominations, one of destruction and one of desolation. What is the abomination of destruction but the one that Antiochus set up there in his time? And what is the abomination of desolation but the universal one, when the Antichrist comes? As Daniel says: “And he will stand for the destruction of many, and he will divide the land as gifts and heap earth upon it, and the land of Egypt will not escape; and these will be saved from his hand: Edom and Moab and the chief of the sons of Ammon.” For these are the ones who will join him because of kinship and will be the first to proclaim him king. Edom are the sons of Esau, who dwell on Mount Seir; Moab and Ammon are the sons of Lot, born of his two daughters. As Isaiah also says: “And they will fly in the ships of foreigners, plundering the sea together, and those from the east and the west and those from the north will give glory, and the sons of Ammon will be the first to obey.”

Proclaimed king by them, glorified by all, and become an abomination of desolation to the world, he will rule for one thousand two hundred and ninety days. As Daniel also says: “And they will set up the abomination of desolation for one thousand two hundred and ninety days. Blessed is the one who endures and reaches one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days.” For when the abomination comes and makes war on the saints, whoever outlasts his days and reaches the further forty-five days, as Pentecost draws near, has attained the kingdom of heaven. For the Antichrist comes into part of the Pentecost, as though he were going to inherit the kingdom together with Christ. That is why Isaiah says: “Let the ungodly be taken away, so that he may not see the glory of the Lord.” And Paul says in the Epistle to the Thessalonians: “whom the Lord Jesus will slay with the breath of his mouth and destroy by the manifestation of his coming.” But it is the saints who are to inherit the kingdom together with Christ.

Since these things are to happen in this way, he added: “And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will arise, some to everlasting life and some to reproach and everlasting shame. And those who understand will shine like the brightness of the firmament, and some of the many righteous like the stars, forever and ever.” Who, then, are those who sleep in the dust of the earth but human bodies? They will receive their own souls back and arise. Some will rise to the resurrection of life, receiving their bodies back pure, radiant and shining like the brightness of the firmament. Others will rise to the resurrection of judgment, receiving them back fit to endure everlasting punishment. As Paul also says: “But he himself will be saved, yet as through fire.” And the Lord said something similar in the Gospel: “Then the righteous will shine as the sun shines in its glory.” And Isaiah says: “Awake, you who sleep, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.” And again the Lord says: “Truly I tell you, the hour is coming and now is when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who have done good will rise to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.” “These,” he says, “will rise to life”: those who have believed in the true life and are written in the book of life. “And these to reproach and everlasting shame”: those who take the side of the Antichrist and are cast with him into everlasting punishment. Isaiah prophesies about him, saying: “As a garment soaked in blood will not be clean, so neither will you be clean, because you have laid waste my land and killed my people. You will not endure for all time, you evil seed. Prepare your children for slaughter for the sins of your father, so that they may not rise and inherit my land.”

After these words Daniel says: “And I looked, and behold, two other men were standing, one on this bank of the river and one on that bank of the river. And they answered the man who was standing above the water of the river and said to him, ‘How long until the end of the wondrous words you have spoken?’ And I heard the man clothed in the baddin, who was above the water of the river, and he raised his right hand and his left hand to heaven and swore by him who lives forever that for a time, times and half a time, when the scattering is completed, they will know all these things.” Who, then, were the two men standing on the bank of the river but the Law and the Prophets? And who was the one standing above the water but the very one they had proclaimed long before? He was to be openly attested by the Father at the Jordan in the last times and shown boldly to the people by John. He is the one who wears the scribe's inkhorn at his waist and the baddin, clothed in the many-colored tunic. They question him because they know that all rule and authority have been given to him, so that they may learn from him exactly when he will bring judgment on the world and when the things he has spoken will be fulfilled. And he, wishing to persuade them in every way, lifted his right hand and his left hand to heaven and swore by him who lives forever. Who swore, and by whom? The Son swore by the Father, saying, “As the Father lives forever, truly, for a time, times and half a time, when the scattering is completed, they will know all these things.” By stretching out his two hands he pointed to his passion.
