By saying “for a time, times and half a time” he indicated the three and a half years of the Antichrist. For by “a time” he means one year, by “times” two years, and by “half a time” half a year. These are the one thousand two hundred and ninety days that Daniel foretold.

So when the passion is completed and the scattering has taken place, and the Antichrist is present in those days, they will know all these things. Why, then, do you still hesitate over what has been said, O man? How can you disbelieve what the Lord has spoken? His first coming has already happened. The one who then stood above the water and was seen by Daniel has now been revealed to the world. His passion has been made known to all, and the Jewish people have been scattered by the Romans. Consider what is meant by “when the scattering is completed they will know all these things.” The Lord was present among them then and was not recognized by them, so they were scattered into all the world and cast out of their own land. Their enemies made war on them and drove them out of the city of Jerusalem, and they became an object of gloating to all the nations. This happened so that the Lord's gospel might be preached throughout the whole world and all the time be fulfilled. Then the last week will be reached, and the two forerunners of Christ will be sent. After them the abomination of desolation will appear, and the Judge of judges will be revealed from heaven. The resurrection of the saints and of the whole world will take place, the everlasting kingdom will be given to the worthy, and the unquenchable, sleepless fire of the ungodly will be kindled.

After these words the prophet wished to inquire more precisely into what would come after the resurrection, so he answered him and said: “Lord, what will be the last of these things?” And he said: “Go, Daniel, for these words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end, until many are chosen and made white and refined by fire, and the lawless act lawlessly, and the wise understand. And you, go and rest; for there are still days until the fulfillment of the end, and you will rise to your lot at the end of the days.” No one can now describe what God has prepared for the saints. No eye has seen it, no ear has heard it, and it has not entered into the human heart; these are things into which even angels long to look. That is why he said to him: “These words are shut up until the time of the end, until many are chosen and made white and refined by fire.” Who are those who are chosen but those found worthy of the kingdom? And who are those made white but those who believe the word of truth? They are made white by it, cast off the filth of their sins and put on the pure and radiant Holy Spirit from heaven, so that when the Bridegroom comes they may go in with him at once. And who are those refined by fire? They are those who pass through fire and water by the spiritual washing of regeneration, and who do the will of God through the fiery trial of many temptations and afflictions. “And the lawless will act lawlessly, and the wise will understand”: some act lawlessly by their free will, while others, again by that same free will, understand and are pleasing to God.

So when the Lord was telling the disciples about the coming kingdom of the saints, how glorious and wonderful it would be, Judas was astonished at what he heard and said: “Who, then, will see these things?” And the Lord said: “Those who have become worthy will see these things.” See now, O man: things that were sealed long ago and could not be known are now proclaimed openly from the housetops. The book of life has already been stretched out and unrolled openly on the wood of the cross. It bears a title written in Latin, Greek and Hebrew, so that Romans, Greeks and Hebrews alike may be taught. Then people who look for the good things to come may believe what is written in this book of life, which has also been preached in the whole world. And when they learn of the evils that are coming, they may fear the judgment and escape everlasting punishment. So may we all be found worthy of the King and receive him, the pure one, with pure bodies and souls, our bodies clothed in bright and fragrant robes and our lamps trimmed with clear oil. Then we will not be deceived by carousing and drunkenness and every illusion and pleasure of this life. We will not think that temporary, earthly and perishable things are greater than the eternal, imperishable and undefiled goods, and so doze off and fall away from eternal life. God is able to make all of us watchful for what is to come, to make us complete, to have mercy on us, to save us, and to guard and keep us from every temptation and affliction. Then we will escape the judgment by fire that is coming and come with joy to meet the appearing of his beloved Child, Jesus Christ our Lord, glorifying him; for to him be glory, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
